lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Remove date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not standard on U.S. resumes and can expose you to age- or nationality-related bias.

items.says: Update the dates or degree status because June 2025 has passed.
items.because: Make clear whether the MBA was awarded rather than leaving it looking like a projected completion date.

items.says: Use consistent date separators throughout the document.
Keep the degree naming and punctuation consistent with the MBA entry.
Clarify whether the internship was full-time if that is not obvious in your recruiting context.
Clarify whether 35% is a relative increase or a percentage-point increase.
Add the baseline, final rate, sample size, or measurement period if available.
Reconsider 'for all merchants' unless the change was genuinely deployed across the entire merchant base.
items.because: It may conflict with language elsewhere about pilots and opt-in groups.

items.says: Clarify your role in deciding, designing, testing, or shipping the change.
items.because: The current line emphasizes the product change more than your contribution.

items.says: Ensure the result was measured rather than inferred.
Specify the scale or impact of the shipped feature, not only that it shipped ahead of plan.
Clarify whether you owned the requirements, facilitated agreement, or contributed as part of a team.
'Two weeks ahead of plan' is useful only if the original timeline was meaningful and documented.
Standardize the list punctuation around engineering, risk, and support.
Change the spelling to U.S. English.
items.because: The resume currently mixes U.S. context with forms such as 'analysed'.

items.says: Format the monetary amount consistently as currency rather than spelling it out.
Clarify whether the loss estimate was annualized from six months of data and what population it covered.
Tighten the relationship between the analysis and the roadmap decision.
items.because: The current ending is grammatically awkward and makes the business case sound like an appositive rather than a clear outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether 140 tickets were personally resolved, coordinated to resolution, or closed by the team.
items.because: The current wording may overstate individual ownership.

items.says: Add the starting and ending queue size if available; 'by half' is less informative without scale.
Specify whether the tickets were defects, support requests, or onboarding blockers.
Rework substantially or remove.
items.because: Opt-in users and non-opt-in users are likely systematically different, so this comparison has selection bias.

items.says: Do not imply this was an A/B test unless users were randomly assigned.
State the analytical limitation or use a more credible evaluation method if one was available.
This bullet currently describes a method without giving a result, so it is weaker than the surrounding bullets.
If retained, place it next to the onboarding outcome bullet because they concern the same initiative.
Clarify your specific ownership of the redesign.
Define the measurement window and whether the reduction was median time across the full pilot cohort.
Explain whether the 2,300 merchants were all new merchants in the pilot or the total eligible population.
Confirm that the result is not based solely on the biased opt-in comparison described in the prior bullet.
Avoid duplicating this accomplishment anywhere else on the resume.
Delete this bullet.
items.because: It describes changing the denominator rather than improving delivery performance.

items.says: The language suggests metric manipulation and may raise ethical concerns.
Clarify whether 30% is relative or absolute.
Add the measurement period and baseline error rate if available.
Confirm whether both sites achieved the result or whether 30% is an aggregate.
Correct the tense inconsistency because the role is in the past.
items.because: The bullet uses 'prepares' instead of past tense.

items.says: Add an outcome, scale, or quality improvement. As written, this is primarily a responsibility rather than an accomplishment.
Specify the scope of the forecast, such as regions, revenue, shipment volume, or business units, if not confidential.
Clarify whether you prepared the pack personally or owned coordination across contributors.
Standardize whether numbers below 10 are written as numerals or words.
Clarify how the 1,800-hour annual saving was calculated and whether it was projected or realized.
Add the operational or financial consequence of the saved hours if available.
Confirm whether the rollout covered all intended depots or only an initial phase.
Confirm whether 'Present' is still accurate.
Clarify whether this was a school project, independent venture, nonprofit initiative, or student organization. 'Student Venture' may be too broad.
Clarify whether 3,100 students registered, had access, or actively used the app.
Explain how the nine-ton figure was measured or estimated.
Use U.S. English and units consistently; consider whether the target audience will expect U.S. customary or metric units.
Clarify your individual product contribution rather than attributing the full launch solely to the title.
Confirm that the dining-hall count remained two throughout the first-year measurement period.
Clarify whether the interviews directly identified missed windows as the main problem.
Establish whether the increase in weekly active users can reasonably be attributed to reminders or whether other launches, marketing, or seasonal effects occurred.
Add the time span represented by 'the following term.'
Vary the underlying emphasis during editing so the bullets do not feel repetitive, while retaining the facts.
items.because: Because the prior bullet also begins with a launch.

items.says: Clarify whether the system was software, a workflow, or a scheduling process.
Define what 'staff cover shifts' means; an external recruiter may not understand it.
Add the measurement period for the 95% fill rate.
Confirm whether the reduction from 10 to two was weekly and sustained.
Consider clarifying the team size and your leadership scope.
Add a concrete purpose, deliverable, or result.
items.because: As written, this is a meeting activity rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify how many clinics or managers were involved.
Make your contribution as team lead more explicit.
Change the passive construction so your team’s ownership is clear, but do not overstate personal responsibility.
Add measurable impact, such as reduced intake time, fewer fields, lower abandonment, or staff adoption.
Clarify whether the changes were piloted, fully implemented, or merely accepted.
Explain what analysis supported shortening the form.
Standardize number treatment with the rest of the resume.
Delete from this section.
items.because: It is unrelated to a hospital network and duplicates the Harbor Payments onboarding accomplishment.

items.says: Reconsider 'A/B testing' unless you have actually designed, run, or interpreted randomized experiments.
items.because: The opt-in comparison described in the experience section is not an A/B test.

items.says: Add proficiency levels only if they communicate meaningful differences and can be defended.
If you use SQL, product-design tools, BI tools, or prototyping tools competently, include them; their absence may be noticeable for product roles.
Excel is relevant, but the resume should show analytical use somewhere in the experience if it is meant to be a selling point.
Use one date style and one dash style throughout.
Use U.S. English consistently: spelling, currency, and measurement conventions.
Keep bullets to approximately one or two lines where possible; several currently wrap to three lines.
Use consistent number rules, especially for small numbers such as two, three, four, and six.
Use consistent serial commas in lists.
Distinguish clearly between realized, projected, and annualized results.
For percentage improvements, specify whether they are relative percentages or percentage-point changes.
Order bullets by impact, not by chronology within each role.
Audit every metric for source, denominator, timeframe, and attribution before submitting.
Ensure the final document is one page unless you have substantial additional experience not shown here.
